recipes: Soak soya chunks 2 hours ahead. Cooking about 25-30 min (estimated - the chef states no total time; video is 15 min).

200g soya chunks (soaked 2 hrs). Spice powder: 2 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp pepper, 1 tsp cumin, 1.5 tsp fennel, 20g dry coconut - dry roast 2 min, grind, then grind in 3 tsp roasted gram. Also: 3 tbsp groundnut oil, 5-6 dry red chillies, 75g shallots, 2-3 green chillies, curry leaves, 1 onion, 2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tomato, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp chilli powder, 3/4 tsp garam masala, salt, coriander leaves.

Dry-roast and grind the spice powder. | Fry red chillies, shallots, green chillies, curry leaves; add onion, then ginger-garlic paste. | Add tomato, turmeric, coriander and chilli powders with 200ml water; cook the masala semi-dry, about 5 min, adding a little oil. | Add strained soya chunks, 2 tsp of the spice powder, coriander leaves; splash of water, flash-cook 2 min on high flame.
Full recipe from the video's own English subtitles (published 2 Aug 2024). Serve as a starter, evening snack with tea, or with rasam rice.

Bread slices (day-old works best), 1 cup besan/gram flour (250ml), 1 onion, 1 tomato, capsicum, 2 green chillies, coriander leaves, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 1 tsp ajwain, water, oil.

Mix the chopped vegetables with the spices; crush the ajwain in. | Add besan, then water little by little to a thick batter. | Spread on bread slices; toast on an oiled tawa on medium flame till crisp both sides.
Ingredients from the video description; steps from the video's captions (posted 20 Oct 2026).
2 ripe bananas, 1 egg, 150g jaggery (about 1 cup), 1 cup wheat flour/atta (250ml cup), 1/2 cup boiled and cooled milk, a pinch of salt, a pinch of cooking soda, butter.

Blend banana, egg and jaggery to a creamy mix. | Add wheat flour and milk; mix in salt and cooking soda; thin with a little milk if too thick. | Cook ladles of batter on a buttered tawa, medium flame, covered, till golden both sides.

Eggs (number not written in the description - shown in the video), 2 cloves garlic, 2 green chillies, 1 onion, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chilli powder, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp cumin powder, salt, coriander leaves.
Method is shown in the video (not written in the description): spiced onion-chilli mix folded into beaten eggs, cooked as an omelette.

Ingredients from the video description (premiered 5 Jan 2025). German channel; the video has no spoken instructions, it is a visual cook-along. Dip uses mayonnaise (usually contains egg - skip it or use eggless mayo for strict veg).

Chef states: 3 whistles (8-10 min) + 10 min rest, then 20 min resting after tempering is mixed in. Active work ~15 min. Total ~45-50 min including rests (estimated total; chef gives segment times only). Video published Oct 8, 2020.

1/2 cup moong dal + 1/2 cup rice (fresh-harvest rice preferred), 3 3/4 cups water (same cup measure), 1/4 tsp ghee. Tempering: 100g ghee (chef's quantity for ~600g cooked mix; reducible), 1 1/4 tsp black pepper, 3/4 tsp jeera (cumin), 30-40g peeled chopped ginger, generous cashew nuts, 30 ml (3 tbsp) thick hing water (asafoetida gum soaked 30 min in hot water, squeezed), handful fresh tender curry leaves, salt to taste.

Wash moong dal and rice together 2-3 times and strain completely. | Add to cooker with 3 3/4 cups water and 1/4 tsp ghee; cook 3 whistles (8-10 min). | Rest 10 min without opening (cooking completes in the rest). | Heat ghee, add pepper and let it pop (stand back), add jeera, then ginger; fry till raw smell goes. | Add cashews, fry to golden; add 3 tbsp thick hing water and curry leaves; raise flame and boil so they mix. | Pour tempering over the cooked rice-dal, add salt, mix well, top with a little ghee, close lid and rest undisturbed 20 min.

Full recipe from the video's own English subtitles (published 8 Oct 2020). Ghee quantity is chef's preference; he says reduce or skip. Use fresh (not wilted) curry leaves and fully peeled ginger per chef's tips.
Pongal Gotsu (brinjal-moong dal side for pongal)
Chef states 5-7 min cooking for the brinjal-onion-tomato stage; total ~20-25 min (estimated total; chef gives segment times only). Same video as Ven Pongal, published Oct 8, 2020.

Gotsu powder (roast in 1 tsp groundnut oil on low flame, then grind fine): 2 1/2 tsp gram dal, 1 1/2 tsp urad dal, 2 tsp dhaniya (coriander) seeds, 8 round red chillies, 1/4 tsp fenugreek seeds (do not exceed - bitter), little more than 1/2 tsp hing added off heat. Base: 2 tbsp sesame oil, mustard seeds, curry leaves, 75g small peeled onions (skippable), 1 chopped tomato, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 brinjal cut in small cubes, water, 1 1/4 ladle thick tamarind water (50g tamarind soaked in hot water, squeezed), salt (add only at the end), 1 tsp crushed jaggery (optional), 2 tsp of the ground powder, 100g boiled moong dal + 1 tumbler water, coriander leaves.

Roast and grind the gotsu powder. | Heat sesame oil, pop mustard, add curry leaves and onions; cook till slightly brown. | Add tomato and turmeric, then brinjal cubes with some water; cook 5-7 min on high flame until soft (no salt yet or brinjal won't cook well). | Add tamarind water, then salt and jaggery. | Stir in 2 tsp of the powder (dals thicken it). | Add boiled moong dal and a tumbler of water; bring to a slight boil only. | Finish with coriander. Target consistency: thicker than sambar, not as thick as kurma.
Full recipe from the video's own English subtitles (published 8 Oct 2020). Chef notes onion and tomato are both optional by family style; brinjal can be flame-roasted and mashed for a smoky version.

Soak urad dal 1 hour at room temperature + 1 hour refrigerated (mixer method; skip refrigeration if using a stone grinder). Frying 5-6 min per batch. Total ~2.5 hours including soaking, ~30 min active (estimated split; chef states soak and fry times). Video published Jun 18, 2020.

150g good-quality urad dal (wash 5 times to remove white residue), water for grinding (~6 tbsp total), 1/2 tsp hing (asafoetida), little more than 1/2 tsp salt, finely chopped ginger (quantity to taste), chopped green chillies, oil for deep frying. Chef: ginger, green chilli, salt and hing are the only essentials; onion/curry leaves/jeera/red chilli/rice powder/soda are optional variations.

Wash urad dal 5 times; soak 1 hour at room temperature, then refrigerate 1 more hour (mixer method only). | Grind without soaking water: 15 seconds, loosen with a spoon, add 2 tbsp water; repeat grinding and add water 3 times total (~6 tbsp) until a fine, soft, puffy paste. | Transfer to a round bowl; add hing, salt, ginger, green chillies. | Beat well to incorporate air for a fluffy batter. | Fry immediately - do not refrigerate the batter or leave it out more than 30 min or vadas absorb oil. | Shape vadas with a hole in the middle (hole lets oil roast the sides evenly); fry on high flame 5-6 min, flipping, till golden brown. | Drain and serve. Same vada works for vada sambar; soak in hot water and drain before adding curd for dahi vada.

Full recipe from the video's own English subtitles (published 18 Jun 2020). Chef: stone grinder gives the softest result; urad dal quality is the biggest factor. Batter must be fried within ~30 min of making.

Batter rests 30 minutes; each dosa roasts on slow flame (a few minutes per dosa; exact per-dosa time not stated). Total ~45 min including resting (estimated total; chef states the 30-min rest). Video published Aug 14, 2020.

Measured with one cup/bowl used for everything: 1 cup plain upma rava (sooji) - keep a handful aside for later, 3/4 cup rice flour, 3/4 cup maida, salt, 1 tsp sugar (for caramelized colour), handful chopped cashews, 1 tsp jeera, 1 tsp pepper, finely chopped ginger, green chillies and curry leaves, 4 cups water first + 1 more cup water and the reserved rava after resting, 1/2 tsp hing. Finely chopped onions for the tawa; oil/ghee for roasting (be generous). Optional: idli molaga podi sprinkled on top.

Whisk rava, rice flour, maida, salt, sugar, cashews, jeera, pepper, ginger, green chillies, curry leaves with 4 cups water until lump-free; rest 30 min (rava expands and thickens). | After resting, add the reserved handful of rava, 1/2 tsp hing and 1 more cup water (5 cups total) for a thin pouring consistency. | Heat tawa, spread oil, sprinkle finely chopped onions and roast slightly. | Stir batter well each time, then pour from the corners inward so holes form. | Cook ONE side only on slow flame until crispy bits appear on top (high flame burns the underside and keeps it soft). | Add ghee/oil generously on top; optionally sprinkle molaga podi; roast to golden brown, fold and serve.

Full recipe from the video's own English subtitles (published 14 Aug 2020). Chef's keys: same cup for all measures, reserved rava added after resting for hotel texture, slow-flame one-side roasting. Pairs with Khara Pudina Chutney (same video).

Hello and welcome to Venkatesh Bhat’s Idhayam Thotta Samayal presented by Idhayam. I will be using Idhayam Sesame oil and Idhayam Groundnut oil to prepare a wide variety of dishes. Co-presented by GRB Ghee, sign of purity. Granulated ghee. Many people have requested for a recipe of Sambar Sadam (rice) which is served at hotels and marriages. This is radically different from Bisibelebath. To make Sambar Sadam, we have to prepare a separate powder. This powder is different from the powder that is used to make Hotel Sambar. So, there are a couple of ingredients which are very fundamental for its flavour, let’s see what they are. Firstly, let’s see how to prepare the Sambar powder. Light the stove. Measurements are very important so make sure you get them right. I will be using this bowl as reference since some of you have told me not to express it in terms of grams. So, in this bowl, I’m going to take a heap of Red Chillies. In the same bowl, take 1 ½ bowl of Coriander seeds. Again, in the same bowl, take ¼ bowl (4 tbsp) of toor dal. Then add 4 tbsp of Bengal gram. After that, 4 tbsp of Urad dal. These 3 dals together will amount to around 1 bowl. I’m not going to add any oil when roasting them. Actually, roasting this in 2 spoons of Groundnut oil will be super. But you’ll have to finish that within 15 days. After that, it will start giving out the stench of oil. However, if you don’t add oil and just dry roast it, this powder will last a month in an airtight container. All the ingredients have to be roasted well for around 5 minutes on medium/high flame. (Make sure to keep stirring) All the ingredients have been more than halfway roasted. At this stage, use a tablespoon and add 2 tbsp full of fenugreek seeds to the same bowl. To it, add 1 ½ tbsp of pepper. Then 1 ½ tbsp of Jeera. The next ingredient is very important. Many people tend to skip this. It is what creates the magic for Sambar Sadam. Add 1 ½ tbsp of Khus-Khus. Add these ingredients after the ingredients in the kadai have roasted halfway through. It will take another 4 minutes for the ingredients to roast well. All the spices have roasted evenly. At this stage, Add a fistful of curry leaves. Then add a full tablespoon of turmeric powder. Add 1 full heaped tbsp of Powdered Hing. Mix well. After you add turmeric powder, Hing and curry leaves, give a brief stir and turn the gas off. This is because the heat of the kadai is sufficient to cook them. If the heat is too high, they will burn. That’s it, ready. Now this has to be ground to a completely fine powder. Observe the bright colour. All the ingredients we roasted have been ground to this fine powder. This is the Sambar powder that we want. Using this to prepare Sambar Sadam will be very good. If you use this powder to prepare Tiffin Sambar, it will be like the sambar in Sambar Sadam. Many people actually prefer this. So, you can go ahead and use this for Tiffin Sambar as well. It is a fantastic all-in-one Sambar powder. I have lit a stove and kept a kadai ready here. Here I have taken 1 ½ cup (around 300g) and 200g of Toor dal which have been cooked in a cooker for 6 whistles along with turmeric powder. After 6 whistles, it has turned out mashy like so. Keep in mind, when cooking, water should 3 times in quantity as compared to Rice and Toor dal put together. (Ex: If rice and toor dal are 2.5 cups put together, then 7.5 cups of water must be added) It will turn out in this consistency. Keep this cooked mixture aside. Here, I have tamarind water that has been obtained by soaking (30 mins) and squeezing 75g of tamarind in 150g of hot water. Now, the pan has heated up. I’m adding 2 tbsp of Mantra Groundnut oil for its flavour. Then I’m adding 2 tbsp of GRB ghee. To it, add 4-5 round red chillies. 1 tsp of mustard. After it pops, add ¼ tsp of Fenugreek seeds. A fistful of curry leaves. 150g of small onions. Then add 1 medium size cubed onion. As it cooks well, add 1 drumstick cut into 2-inch pieces and roast well. Drumstick takes a lot of time to cook. That is why we’re adding it a bit early so that When we pour water later, it will cook fully. I will be adding vegetables such as drumstick, carrot, beans etc. You may add pumpkin, flat beans, brinjal, lady’s finger, potato etc. It is all up to you. You may add any vegetable that you would like to be present in the Sambar Sadam. Avoid cauliflower, green peas etc. The drumstick and onions have roasted well. At this stage, Add 4 chopped beans. 2 diced carrots. Mix well. As it cooks, Add 3 cubed tomatoes. Cooking the tomatoes and other vegetables in the oil beforehand, will infuse the flavour of Sambar Sadam inside them as well. That is why I’m doing this. You may cook them all at once in a cooker and then add. This has to be cooked for around 5-7 minutes on medium flame. It has roasted well. At this stage, add ½ tsp of turmeric powder. Then pour ½ litre of water. Turn the gas to ‘high’ and let it cook for 7-8 minutes. 10 minutes have passed since I poured the water. Because of that, the drumstick has cooked well. At this stage, add 100ml of tamarind water. Don’t add too much or else it will be sour. Add required salt and 50g of jaggery. Just like how fenugreek seeds signify bitterness, chillies signify spiciness, etc. Sweetness is signified by either sugar or jaggery. That is why a little bit of jaggery is required for a very subtle sweetness. At this stage, add the cooked rice and toor dal mixture. Slow down the gas and mix well. Break all lumps, if present. It has to be brought to a boil. That’s it. Everything has mixed well together. At this stage, add 2 tbsp of Sambar powder we prepared and a handful of coriander leaves. Mix well so that the powder mixes in the rice mixture. If you want to mix it easily, dissolve the sambar powder in ½ tumble of water and add the same. Make sure the sambar powder is mixed fully. Next, I’m going to open a jar of GRB ghee. And add 3 tbsp of ghee. Turn the gas off. Garnish with a handful of coriander. Close it with a lid and do not disturb it for 15 minutes. After 15 minutes, serve it with Urulai (potato) roast or something crunchy. Fantastic Sambar Sadam! Only on ‘Idhayam Thotta Samayal’ presented by Idhayam, In Venkatesh Bhat style. Enjoy!

Hello and welcome to Venkatesh Bhat’s Idhayam Thotta Samayal. I will be using Idhayam Sesame oil and Idhayam Groundnut oil to prepare a wide variety of dishes. I’m going to prepare fantastic Mushroom Dum Biriyani that can be prepared at home. Firstly, good quality long grain basmati rice. I have first washed the Basmati rice and then let it soak in water for 20 mins. Let that be here. Normally I’d say this will serve 4 people, but quantity is subjective and may differ for different people. So, let me put it this way. I’m making enough biriyani for it to fill this pan to the brim. For that, we will require ½ kg of basmati rice. The pan has heated. To it, add 4 tbsp of ghee. 4 cloves. 4 pieces of cinnamon. 6 green Elaichis. 3 Black Elaichis. Some Javitri Spice. 2-3 bay leaves. ½ tsp of Biriyani Jeera/Shahi Jeera. As it is crackling, slice 3 onions Many of you have asked for a video on cutting techniques. So, observe, this is slicing. The thumb is on the backside while the index and middle fingers are in the front while being angled backwards. It is important to hold this angle else the knife will cut your finger. Learn this technique slowly and patiently. Don’t try to speed it up and harm yourself in the process. Even though I’ve been doing this for 30 years, I still cut myself now and then. When I was working at Taj Coromandel, Mr. Nataraj was the executive chef. The first aid kit was available only in his office so you’d have to request him for a bandage if you cut yourself. So, I’ve sliced 3 onions and am adding them right now. Cook them well and let them turn juicy. They needn’t turn golden brown. So, as I was saying, he’d tie the bandage if we injured ourselves. But he used to say this ‘If you cut yourself once, you’re a hard worker but if you cut yourself twice, you’re useless’ Because of this, we’d never report our injuries the second time out of fear of being reprimanded by him. So be careful. You may cut yourself often. If it’s a deep cut, visit the doctor. But if it is just a small bruise, smear turmeric powder over it and let it lay for a while. But if you’re unsure, it is best to visit a doctor. Onions have cooked well. Next, we have to add tomatoes. Take 3 medium size tomatoes and slice it like so. If you cut this way, they are called slices. But if you do it this way, they are quarters. And this way is called chops. If you cook it even further, it is called ‘frying to golden brown consistency’ If you cook it lightly and add other ingredients, it is called sautéing the onions. It is past the sauté stage and is frying well. All the spices mixed with oil, along with the fried onions give out a fantastic aroma! In the previous video, I demonstrated how to prepare homemade Garam Masala. So, I’m going to use the same garam masala to prepare this Biriyani. The onions have cooked juicily. At this stage, I have some ginger garlic paste here (60% garlic 40% ginger) Add 2 tbsp of ginger garlic paste.  This is very important for Biriyani. Even if you add little more, the taste will be enhanced. For 3 onions, I have added 3 tomatoes and 2 tbsp of ginger garlic paste. All the ingredients have cooked well together. At this stage, Slit and add 4 dark colored green chillies OR 3 light colored green chillies. This is important as well and is to be added when the raw smell of the ginger garlic paste goes away. Cook briefly for 2 mins and add the tomatoes and let it cook. At this stage, add ½ tsp of turmeric powder. 1 ½ heaped tsp of Kashmiri chilli powder. Then, required salt for the Biriyani Masala. Mix everything. Before it changes colour, pour ½ tumbler of water and boil so that everything combines. In the boiling stage, add mushrooms. If they are big, cut them into 2. Make sure they are washed well since they’re usually covered with soil and dirt. You may soak it in water and Maida, then let running water pass on it. This will remove the dirt. If you don’t prefer the stalk, you may remove it. This is Mushroom Dum Biriyani which is why I’m adding mushroom. You may add anything else as well such as potato, cauliflower. It will turn out to be a type of ‘Tahri’, a dish from UP side. It utilizes only potato and cauliflower. You may also use carrot, beans, green peas etc. As the mushroom cooks, I have some thick beat curd here. Add 6 tbsp. It is about 1- ½ ladles. Let the masala cook well. If you boil it for 2 minutes, it can even serve as a side dish for chapati! Let it boil. Here I have some boiling water. I’m adding around 250g of Basmati rice to it. The Masala we’ve prepared is sufficient for ½ kg of rice. So, I’m going to take some masala out from this, and only add 250g of the boiled rice. So, if you have a bigger pan, you may add 0.5 kg rice and cook with the whole masala. After adding the rice, add ½ tsp of ghee. Then add half a bunch of pudina. Half a bunch of coriander leaves. Mix well. It is to be removed when it is half cooked i.e., around 5 minutes. When all these ingredients mix together, the rice will obtain a distinct combined flavour. At that stage, add the required salt for the rice. Assuming you added the rice in piping hot boiling water, you may remove it after 5 minutes. The rest of the cooking will take place with the Masala in the dum method. It has cooked halfway through. Strain the rice and keep it aside. The Biriyani masala is ready. At this stage, I’m 1 full tsp of the Garam masala I prepared in the previous video. Cook for 1 minute. Like I said before, this pan can only accommodate 250g of rice so I’m going to take some masala out. This much is sufficient. At this stage, add the half-done rice. Don’t mix after adding the rice. Just spread it around. It has to cook for 30 minutes in the dum method. Place the whole thing atop a dosa tawa (nonstick, regular etc.) Turn the gas to high so that the tawa heats up. Add chopped pudina and chopped coriander. Add fried onions. Roasted cashew nuts. Saffron milk. Dum biriyani is a dish from the Awadh cuisine and has a lot of flavouring agents. Add ½ tsp of kewra water. (Don’t add too much, the smell will be too strong) Add ghee on the sides and in the middle (3 tbsp or as per your preference) Close it with an airtight lid. Roll chapati or poori dough. (This is optional and is a hotel method) This is used for sealing the lid to completely block air. Seal the lid. Lower the flame to the lowest level and let it cook for 25 minutes. After 25 minutes, let it rest for 10 minutes. After that, if you open it, you will have an absolute marvel in front of you. Ah! All the flavoring agents have combined together to give a fantastic colour and aroma! It resembles the face of a person after his parents have agreed for a love marriage! Mix it like so, and transfer it. Each grain of rice is noticeable! This is the advantage of dum cooking, the water will drain correctly and each grain will be noticeable. Notice how well the mushrooms have cooked. People will be surprised at the fact that this biriyani was prepared at home. Garnish with coriander leaves, cashew nuts, brown onions. Decorate it with some tomato slices. ½ tsp of ghee. More coriander. Excellent mushroom biriyani, dum cooking style, from the north western frontier. Authentic dum cooking involves the burning of charcoal, we have used a normal flame. So that method is even more flavourful. Or else, in the Galouti kebab video, I followed a method of using a charcoal piece and adding ghee and closing it. You may follow that as well. I followed this method for it to be home-friendly, hence ‘dum cooking’. Excellent Mushroom Dum Biriyani just for you on Venkatesh Bhat’s Idhayam Thotta Samayal. Enjoy!

People always say that it is a pre-existing talent or you must have a knack for it, but that’s not true. Having a knack for cooking is nothing but knowing the cooking time for each ingredient. For example, for Chana dal, it should be cooked thoroughly on low flame till it changes colour. Saunf, on the other hand, should be roasted briefly. Mustard has to be roasted till it pops. Here I have regular raw rice. Add 2 tsps. And a handful of curry leaves. The reason for the addition of rice is to give a mild pasty consistency. This is optional. I personally prefer the thickness provided to the gravy by these rice grains after grinding. That is why I’m choosing to add it. Each ingredient has cooked well individually with a beautiful colour. 7-8 minutes have passed (slow flame) since I started cooking all these ingredients. The beauty of Vatha Kuzhambu lies in the fact that it won’t rot even after a week since it doesn’t have coconut in it. Add a handful of curry leaves. The right colour has been obtained. At this stage, Add ½ tsp of turmeric powder ½ tsp of Kashmiri Red chilli powder. Here I have tamarind water. But there are some recipes which have some tasks that must not be rushed such as grinding, cooking separately etc. I have read many comments which have asked if it is okay to add all the ingredients at once and cook. This is wrong because each ingredient has to cook in a certain temperature to get the required flavour. This holds true for order of ingredients and cooking as well. So kindly follow the exact procedure for the perfect end product. On that note, I’ve decided to show you easy recipes throughout the entirety of this month. Furthermore, these items are storable for future consumption. So I have planned some soup varieties, continental, Indian rice varieties etc. The first dish I’m showing is Pudina Sadam (rice). There are different types of rice, but Pudina rice, curry leaves rice, Podi rice etc are popular among all age groups. The chutney that we will be preparing for Pudina Sadam can be refrigerated for 7-10 days. So, you may toss it with rice whenever you want. It is almost like Puliyodharai Mix! Let me show you the same, in a tasty and exciting manner! Fantastic Pudina rice, let’s see how to do it. Firstly, Heat a kadai. We are going to roast some ingredients and grind them to a paste which will then be mixed with rice. I’m going to use sesame oil to prepare this chutney. However, during the rice mixing part, I will use ghee. I’m adding 2 tbsp of Idhayam Sesame oil. 1 tbsp of Urad dal. Many of you ask me the difference between a tablespoon and teaspoon. Observe closely. This is a teaspoon. And this, is a tablespoon. The urad dal has changed colour. At this stage, Add 4 slit green chillies. To it, add a few curry leaves. A handful of peeled garlic cloves. I’m adding 3 bunches of cleaned and chopped Pudina leaves, with their stems removed. Let the Pudina leaves roast well in the high heat. It will give out a fantastic aroma and flavour as it cooks with the other ingredients. There are many variants. Some people even add coriander leaves to this. But I prefer to isolate the flavour of Pudina instead of letting the strong coriander taste take over. The speciality for this dish, is that the rice will contain some partially cooked chopped onions which greatly enhance the flavour of the dish. So, we will have to keep 2-3 onions chopped and ready, so that we get bits of onions with each spoonful. Let it saute well. Some people add coconut, skip garlic etc. I have added garlic but you may avoid it if you want. Instead, you may add a handful of coconut at this stage for the thickness. All that’s left is to add tamarind water, and to grind it. Then the chutney will be ready. The problem with using coconut is that, you can only store it in the refrigerator for 2 days. By the 3rd day, it will rot. That is why I’m using garlic and not coconut in this recipe, so that it can be stored for up to 10 days in the refrigerator. The pudina has sautéed well. At this stage, turn the gas off. Here I have thickly squeezed tamarind water. Add 5 tbsps. (50g of tamarind soaked and squeezed in 150ml of warm water) Once it cools down, grind it to a fine paste. The fine paste is ready, Like I said, we haven’t added coconut in this. Let’s see how to prepare the rice using this chutney. Like I said, you can store this for up to 10 days in the refrigerator. This is the right consistency. Heat a kadai and add 2 ½ tbsp of ghee. You may alter the quantity. To it, add 1 tsp of mustard. Once it crackles, add 1 tsp of Urad dal. Let it turn golden brown. Once it changes colour, I’m adding a handful of cashew nuts. You may increase or decrease the quantity. When it turns light golden brown, add a few curry leaves. 1 tsp of chopped garlic. (Avoid if you don’t consume garlic) The flavour of roasted chopped garlic is heavenly! It has turned golden brown; Add chopped onions. Here I have 250g of rice here cooked in a cooker using 3 tumblers of water. Usually for rice varieties like this, one may follow two methods. If you’re cooking in a cooker, cooking it in 1:2 ½ water ratio will make the rice slightly mashy. Another alternative, is to take excess water (6-8 tumblers of water for 1 tumbler of rice) and bring it to a boil. Once it is boiling, add the soaked rice and cook it 75% through. It will turn out puffy, and is best suited for rice varieties like these. The onions shouldn’t cook too much, I have just sauteed them for 2 mins so that it halfway cooked. At this stage, add the ground chutney. I’m adding 5 tbsp. Mix well. Add salt as per taste for the dish. You may have this chutney mixture with dosa, rava dosa, Kuli Paniyaram etc. It has mixed well. At this stage, add the boiled rice. Toss well. Its flavour is akin to the tempting aroma of green chutney in street food stalls! Garnish with 1 ½ tsp of ghee to brighten it up! Toss again. Turn the gas off once tossed. Excellent Pudina Rice! If chutney is ready, then the only work is to cook the rice and season it. Have this with a papad and a bowl of curd! More than enough. Have it before 8pm and be careful not to eat biriyani dishes after 8pm. Actually 7pm is the limit but let's be lenient here. And most importantly, don’t lie down within 3 hours of eating dinner. Take care of your health in this COVID situation. Eat healthy good and have oil fried dishes only once in a while. Taste is very important, but so is health. Enjoy the cooking, enjoy the dishes. Hello and welcome to Venkatesh Bhat’s Idhayam Thotta Samayal. Today we’re looking at another heavily requested fantastic dish. It is very easy, but the conundrum is achieving hotel style taste at home. It is a very simple technique and further, this dish relies heavily on precise measurements. So, it is very easy to achieve hotel style taste at home. Fantastic Onion Rava Dosa! I’m going to use onion and prepare Rava dosa. If you wish, you may skip onion and prepare plain Rava dosa. Even that will turn out good. Speaking of Rava Dosa, In Durga lunch home, Evening timings were from 6 p.m. to 11 p.m. It was a very small restaurant and could accommodate only around 50 people. Teynampet Signal was at the end of Pondy Bazar. Durga lunch home was situated in that vicinity. It ran for around 30-35 years, after being started by my grandfather, passed on to my father and then to me. After which, I came out of that business. So, in those 6-7 years I was actively involved in the hotel after studying hotel management. At that time, Naidu Hall was a very popular place. The owners used to order 25-30 Rava Dosas on every working day as parcel. That is how intense the fame of Onion Rava dosa and onion chutney was. Before this, I had demonstrated onion chutney and coconut chutney in a previous episode. Onion Rava Dosa is the perfect companion to those chutneys. So, I will teach you how to make that Onion Rava Dosa today. Now, I’m going to use this bowl for all my measurements. You may also use any type of measuring vessel. But, make sure to take all other ingredients with respect to the same vessel. 1 bowl of Plain Upma Rava/Sooji. Here I have Rice flour. ¾ bowl of Rice flour. From the 1 bowl of Rava you’ve added, take a handful of Rava and keep it aside. Add the rice flour (¾ cup) Now take ¾ bowl of Maida and add it. Let the handful of Rava stay aside. Add required salt for the batter. 1 tsp of sugar. A handful of chopped cashew nuts. 1 tsp of Jeera. 1 tsp of pepper. Some finely chopped ginger. Finely chopped green chillies. Finely chopped curry leaves. Add all of these and use a whisk to beat them all together using some water. Take the measuring bowl that we previously used, And pour 4 bowls/cups of water. To recap, 1 cup Rava, ¾ cup Maida, ¾ cup Rice flour and 4 cups of water along with other ingredients. Before pouring the batter on the tawa, another cup of water and this handful of Rava from earlier have to be added. So now after adding water, mix until all ingredients are mixed well. Beat well using a whisk so that lumps aren’t formed and everything mixes well. After beating it, keep it aside and let it rest for half an hour. In that half an hour, all the ingredients will gel together and form a thick paste. Rava has a quality of expanding to 4 times its mass when in contact with water. So, if you consume this much Upma, it will expand to this much inside you. So, if we let this Rava rest for 30 minutes, it will expand and get thicker because of the water. The reason for adding Rava again at the end, is because the rough texture of it complements the soft Rava from the batter well. It will give a hotel-like taste. This is very important and we are going to add it at the end. While the batter rests for 30 minutes, let us look at fantastic spicy Pudina chutney which is a really good combo. Let me teach you how to prepare it. Light the stove and heat a pan. To it, add 3 spoons of oil. Some Jeera. A handful of Chana dal. A handful of Urad dal. A handful of small onions. ½ a handful of peeled garlic cloves. 4 slit green chillies. Let all the ingredients roast well. This chutney shouldn’t be too watery when served, it should be slightly thick. If the chutney is too watery, then the Rava dosa will feel soft. So, to make it thick, we’re adding chana dal and urad dal. Otherwise they’re not required. But the addition of these two, will enhance the crispiness of Rava dosa when eaten together. Cook until all the ingredients turn golden brown. They have fried to a golden brown colour. At this stage, add 1 ½ chopped tomatoes. Let it cook well. The more it cooks, the better it’ll taste. Else, it will give off a raw smell and taste. It has cooked well. At this stage, add ½ spoon of turmeric powder. Some Hing/Asafoetida. Half a bunch of coriander leaves. One full handful of Pudina leaves. Cook it well. As soon as you add the leaves, they will shrink. Cook until the raw smell goes away. It has cooked well with the other ingredients. At this stage, add 2 tbsp of Tamarind water. (50g of tamarind soaked in hot water and squeezed) Cook until raw smell goes away. Pudina, onion and tamarind are the best of friends because their combination is incredible. Mix well and turn off the gas. Add 1 half of grated coconut. Add required salt for chutney. Mix well. (Gas should be off) It is best if consumed on the same day. Else, store it in the fridge and use it the next day. because it contains fresh coconut and small onions so it may turn rancid soon. So do not store it for more than 2 days. If you prepare it today, finish it today or else max by tomorrow afternoon. After mixing it like so, let it cool down. It has to be ground to a fine paste using a mixer. Fantastic Khara Pudina Chutney is ready! Now, let’s prepare a simple seasoning for this chutney. Heat a pan and add 1 spoon of oil. 4 round red chillies. As it roasts lightly, add ½ spoon of mustard. Then add ½ tsp of urad dal. Roast until it turns golden brown. It has turned golden brown, turn off the gas and add some curry leaves. Toss it briefly and add on top of the chutney. Matter over! Fantastic Spicy Pudina chutney is ready! This is onion Rava Dosa’s best friend. Now let me teach you how to prepare Onion Rava Dosa. Chop an onion as fine as possible. It will roast well only if it’s small in size. Now, heat a pan. (I’m using nonstick pan. You may use a regular pan, no problem. The taste isn’t dependent on that) Now, we have the batter which has rested for 30 mins. It has turned thick. This is the result of all the ingredients we added earlier. Now we need to add the handful of Rava which we kept aside earlier, Hing and some more water. Add ½ spoon of Hing. Handful of Rava. Mix it. After mixing it, add 1 cup (previously used cup) of water. So, in total, we’ve added 5 cups of water. Use the same cup you used for other measurements. This is the required consistency for Rava Dosa batter. Now we’re ready to prepare the Dosa. Make sure the pan is heated. Spread some oil across the surface. It will roast well if there is more oil. Take a handful of chopped onions and sprinkle all over the surface. Let it roast slightly in the oil. Mix well before pouring it since some ingredients will have settled at the bottom. (This applies to any dosa batter) If you know how to pour it using a tumbler, super, go ahead. Else I will tell you how to pour it using a ladle. Take a ladle of batter and pour it all around the corners and make your way to the center. There will be holes in between, it will be very aesthetic and good. We have to cook only one side on slow flame. Since the flame is slow, it will roast well. We have added a tsp of sugar in the batter earlier for the purpose of colour since it will caramelize And give a roasted gold colour. If you cook it directly and immediately in high flame, The dosa will be soft and will be burnt on the underside. So, roast it on slow flame till you see crispy bits on top. Now add ghee/oil on top. Add it in excess, only then will it roast well. Let it roast more. Suppose you want to add Molaga Podi (Gunpowder) to Onion Rava Dosa, you may do so at this stage. After it changes colour, fold it and it will be really good. In T. Nagar near Pondy Bazar side, next to Brilliant tutorials, there was a dosa stall. The Podi Rava Dosa there was the best I ever had. It was fantastic! Their speciality is, they add a ghee-oil mixture (less ghee, more oil) on top and sprinkle this much Podi on top. After 2 minutes, the Dosa was folded and served. The flavour was unbelievable! So if you want to add Podi, you may add it at this stage. Let it turn golden brown, then I’ll tell you how to fold it. Observe, it has started turning brown. At this stage, fold it this way, strike the middle and fold it again. Plate the Rava dosa and add some Pudina chutney in a bowl. Sprinkle some onion on top. Fantastic Hotel style Onion Rava Dosa and Khara Pudina chutney! This is Venkatesh Bhat’s Idhayam Thotta Samayal! Hotel style Rava dosa in your home, daily!

Stuffing the brinjal, frying the brinjal in oil etc are all different variations of the recipe. The recipe I’m going to demonstrate, utilises onion and garlic. Avoid onion and garlic if you do not eat them, and simply follow the rest of the recipe. I have incorporated some of my preferences into this recipe such as decreasing the sourness and strengthening the flavour of jaggery. Jaggery is mandatory to balance and make the sourness mild. The quantity however, can be altered as per your preference if you think I’m adding too much. So, I’m going to teach you fantastic Brinjal Kuzhambu in my style. We have to first prepare a masala. The required ingredients are, Firstly, heat a pan. For this Brinjal Kuzhambu, sesame oil is strongly recommended for the best result. So, I’m using Idhayam Sesame oil here. I’ve added 2 tbsp of oil. Now, I’m going to roast some ingredients in this. 1 tsp of fenugreek seeds. Let it roast lightly before adding other ingredients. When it roasts lightly, add 2 tsp of chana dal. When it turns light golden brown, add 3 tsp of peanuts (peeled). The one I’ve used is readymade roasted peanuts. So, there is no need to roast it too much, since it is already roasted. Then, add 5 tsp of coriander seeds. I will be using ½ kg of these small brinjals for this dish. If the brinjals are large, then use around 10, else if they’re small, 20-22 will suffice. I'm preparing the masala for that quantity. The coriander seeds have roasted lightly and their flavour has been brought out. At this stage, Add 3 tsp of white sesame/til seeds and let it crackle. After it crackles, add 4 heaped tsp of grated coconut, and turn the gas off, and toss. This is because the coconut mustn’t change colour. So it is important to turn the gas off after adding coconut. Transfer to a bowl. After it cools down, grind to a paste using ¼ tumbler of water. Now let’s prepare the masala required for the Kuzhambu. I’m adding 4 tbsp of Idhayam Sesame oil. Let it heat. Cut the brinjal like this by making an X mark. This will help you inspect it for any worms. Next, cut half the stalk of the brinjal. Let the remaining stalk, be as is. Cut all the brinjals this way. After the oil has heated, and add the brinjals (make sure they’re dry, else the oil will splutter) Fry it well in the oil for 3 minutes in medium flame. This will cook them 50%. Since brinjal Kuzhambu contains tamarind water and coconut, it will take some time for the brinjals to cook. So, if we let it cook 50% in the oil and then add to the Kuzhambu, it will retain its stiffness and at the same time, be cooked well. The purple colour has obtained a shiny glaze. So, at this stage, reduce the gas slightly, and let it fry. The oil should seep into the cut section of the brinjal and cook it well from the inside. These are all small techniques that greatly help in enhancing the final result almost akin to the taste of marriage feasts, hotels etc. The reason home cooked food differs from restaurants is because of these small techniques which greatly influence the flavour. Resorting to shortcuts, will give you an equivalent subpar taste. It has fried well, about 50%. If you cook it for another 2-3 minutes, it will be mashy and fully cooked. Transfer out only the brinjals and let the oil remain in the Kadai. To the hot oil, add 5-6 round red chillies. As it roasts, add 1 tsp of mustard. As it pops, add garlic. I’m very fond of onion and garlic, so I will be adding a lot. If you wish to skip the addition of garlic, you may do so. So, I’ve added a handful of peeled garlic cloves. Ingredients like garlic, small onions, sesame oil, tamarind, etc are all wonderful ingredients that form an excellent combo! After the garlic roasts to a golden-brown colour, I’ve added 150g of peeled sambar onions/small onions. For people who skip onion and garlic, just avoid adding these two ingredients, and follow the rest of the steps. As the onion roasts, add half a bunch of curry leaves and let it roast. The onion is supposed to roast to a stage past the golden-brown colour for the best flavour. The onion has roasted well. Here I have tomato puree made with 10 tomatoes, but that much isn’t required. Just add 5 medium tomatoes worth of tomato puree. (To prepare the puree, all you need to do is grind the tomatoes to a fine paste) To the boiling puree, add ½ tsp of turmeric powder. 1 ½ heaped tsp of coriander powder. Here I have Kashmiri red chilli powder which gives richer and brighter colour than other chilli powders. I recommend it for this dish. 1 ½ heaped tsp of Kashmiri red chilli powder. Stir well and let it combine. Even though we added a lot of oil, it is not at all apparent since it has been absorbed. All the ingredients have blended together beautifully to form a thick masala. Cooking it for 2 minutes will remove its raw smell. After the raw smell goes away, add the ground paste we prepared earlier. Mix well. Since the ingredients of the paste have already been roasted in oil, there is no need to cook them too much. Just mix and cook till they combine. After it combines, I have some tamarind water ready here. (75g of tamarind soaked and squeezed in 150ml hot water) Pour that 150ml of tamarind water. (75g of tamarind soaked and squeezed in 150ml hot water after straining) Pour 1 – 1 ¼ tumbler of water and let it boil for 6-8 minutes. This is because the ingredients present in the paste are all thickening agents so it is important to pour water And get rid of the raw smell of tamarind by cooking and letting its taste integrate into the dish. Like I said, let it boil for 5-7 minutes. As it boils, add required salt. Then, my favourite, jaggery. Everyone close your eyes! I’m adding a lot, you may add lesser. Mix well. I’ve added a handful (about 100g) of jaggery. You may add 30-50g, it will suffice. Jaggery, salt and tamarind water have to cook well in the gravy for 5-6 minutes. 5-6 minutes have passed and the raw smell has gone away. Observe the consistency, it has reached a thick stage. At this consistency, add the brinjals which we fried earlier. Some oil may have seeped out from the brinjals, don’t let it go to waste. Mix. Since the brinjals have already cooked halfway through earlier, they have to cook for 5 more mins in the gravy. If it has thickened, pour another ½ tumbler of water. Add 1 tsp of Hing/Asafoetida powder and turn the gas down and let it simmer for 5 minutes so that it combines. Within 3-4 minutes, the brinjals will absorb the flavour of the masala and be ready. After that, before taking it out, add 3 tbsp of sesame oil for the magic factor. This is optional. It is for the purpose of a beautiful shine. Adding it, will give a flowing consistency. Additionally, this won’t rot for even a week as long as you keep it refrigerated. So, if you prepare this, the best time to eat it would be the next day. If you eat it the same day, it won’t be the best result. For example, If you prepare it in the morning, you may eat at night, but the best time to eat would be for next day’s lunch or dinner. It will be out of this world. The epitome of its taste will be from the third day onwards. So, you may store it for up to a week in the fridge, and use it as and when required by reheating with some water. You may eat it with rice, curd rice, idly, dosa etc. Superb Brinjal Kuzhambu. Like I said before, there are numerous variations, but this is my style. Fantastic Ennai Kathirikai Kuzhambu, from the kitchens of Idhayam Thotta Samayal, just for you!

Today I will teach you how to prepare Vegetable Biriyani. I will be using Fedora Extra Virgin Olive oil to show you how you can prepare this easily at home. Let’s go to the episode. Many people have requested this dish. ‘Venkatesh Bhat’s Idhayam Thotta Samayal’ is a pure vegetarian channel. I’m very sorry to everyone who requested non-vegetarian dishes. So today I will show you how to prepare Vegetable Biriyani. You may alter the recipe by including meat and following the same procedure. Instead of using ghee/butter to prepare this, I will be using Fedora’s Extra Virgin Olive oil. It is extracted by cold pressing olives grown in Spain which are exposed to minimal sunlight. It is rich in antioxidants and monounsaturated fatty acids. This is better in terms of health quotient if you compare it to regular oil. Fedora has two types of olive oils: 1) Extra Light Olive oil 2) Extra Virgin Olive oil. Extra Virgin olive oil is best for salad, baking, garnishing, dressing etc. It is very good in quality when uncooked. However, Light Olive oil is appropriate for cooking, Be it south Indian, frying, Biriyani and for different cuisines. That is why I’m going to be using this light variant today to prepare Biriyani. Firstly, I’m turning on the range and adding around 6tbsp of Fedora Olive oil. To the oil, firstly add 5-6 cloves. 4-5 Elaichi. 5-6 pieces of cinnamon sticks (broken). 4 Black cardamoms (Badi Elaichi). 2-3 bay leaves. I have kept all the required ingredients ready here such as Onion, Tomato, Vegetables, Garam Masala powder etc. So first, let’s prepare the masala. On this side, I’ve kept water here for boiling. I have some Basmati here that has been soaked in room temperature water for 15-20 minutes. So, I have the soaked basmati rice and boiling water ready. We have to strain the water from the rice. Hello and welcome to Venkatesh Bhat’s Idhayam Thotta Samayal presented by Idhayam. I will be using Idhayam Sesame oil and Idhayam Groundnut oil to prepare a wide variety of dishes. There are still so many items that are yet to be demonstrated. Many of the requested items are uncommon dishes. So at least for the first 200 videos, I’m aiming to demonstrate common daily dishes. I will definitely demonstrate exotic dishes in between just like how I’ve shown dum biriyani, Paneer tikka etc. Continental, Chinese etc. one viewer has repeatedly asked Vangi bath on many videos. I have noted it and will definitely demonstrate it. As soon as I finish the first list of lined up dishes, I will make sure to add that dish in the next iteration. Today, I will be demonstrating the heavily-requested Idly Milagai Podi/powder. Along with it, I will make mini idlis and teach you how to make podi tossed idlis. Idly Milagai powder will go well with idly, dosa or even with rice and ghee. I will be preparing this without adding garlic but some people roast garlic slightly and add it. So, you may do it either way. Addition of garlic will be good if eating with rice. If you’re adding garlic, add unpeeled garlic, roast it and grind into a powder with the other ingredients. But the idly powder I’m going to prepare, won’t have garlic in it. Let me tell you what to do. It is very simple. Just follow the process correctly. Light a stove. Some ingredients have to be roasted in oil while other are to be dry roasted. Let me first dry roast the ingredients. I’m going to take my measurements with respect to this cup. Take ¼ cup of white sesame seeds. You may use black sesame seeds as well. Idhayam’s Sambhandi sesame seeds are an excellent choice since they are even sized and won’t have a speck of dirt. So, add ¼ cup of white sesame seeds. Let it roast slowly. Don’t add sesame directly. The raw taste will be unpleasant. It is mandatory to dry roast it. Observe the colour. It was white at first, now it is light golden colour. Next add ¼ cup (same as sesame seeds) of Chana dal. Dry roast it slowly till it turns golden. It will take 3-4 minutes for it to roast to the required level. And if you add it to a non-heated pan and then try to roast it, it will take 7-8 minutes. Since I’ve added it to a hot pan, I will roast this for about 4 minutes. As much as possible, roast it on low flame and remove it in between and fry using the pan’s heat. Because if it changes colour quickly, the desired flavour of the Chana dal won’t be brought out. The moisture content has to completely disappear for the powder to come out fine. If you store the powder in an airtight container, you may use it for up to a month. Be it podi idly, podi dosa, or just plain idly, dosa etc. It is an easy side dish option when there is no time to prepare chutney. The chana dal has been roasted. Next, add ½ cup of urad dal (or double of that of chana dal) So, if you added 50g of sesame and 50g of chana dal, you will need to add 100g of Urad dal. Let this roast slowly. Chana dal is easier to roast on all side because of its shape. But for Urad dal, make sure to roast till brown on all sides. The slower it cooks and turns colour, the better the flavour of the Milagai powder. So, the degree of roasting of Urad dal and Chana dal is very important in defining the final taste. So, make sure to patiently roast every granule till it turns brown for the best possible Milagai powder. I’ve been constantly stirring this for about 10 minutes on slow flame to avoid it burning. Next, add 1 tsp of Jeera. 1 tsp of pepper. A fist of curry leaves. Dry roast them. After they’ve roasted well, transfer them. Now, I’m adding 1 tbsp of Idhayam Sesame oil. Lower the gas. Break and add about 25g of gum Asafoetida. Fry until the oil covers it on all sides and turns it crispy. 25g will suffice. Let it fry for 4 minutes. This is because it is necessary for it to turn crispy so that it can grind with the other ingredients. Transfer just the Asafoetida out. Let the oil stay in the pan. To the pan, add another ½ tbsp of Sesame oil. After it heats, lower the gas, and add 15 Byadagi chillies. With it, add 10 long regular red chillies. Turn the gas off, and fry it lightly using the pan’s heat. (It shouldn’t change colour) Keep it aside in a separate plate. That’s it, matter over. To the ingredients which have been roasted without oil, add the required salt. Around 1 tsp. Firstly, the red chillies will cool down in about 10 mins. When it cools down, Grind it to as fine of a powder as possible. After it turns to a fine powder, add the rest of the ingredients to the powder and continue grinding for another 2 mins. This is because, only red chillies have to be fine. The rest of the ingredients have to be slightly coarse. Only then, will the colour be bright. So, after it cools down, let me show you how it will look after grinding the chillies to a fine powder, and then the rest of the ingredients coarsely. Observe, the red chillies presence is fine while the rest of the ingredients are coarse. Fantastic Idly powder. This is very good for health since it doesn’t have any additives. Dal and Red chillies help in protein. Asafoetida helps in digestion. Jeera and pepper balance the gas. And then since it is prepared using sesame oil, it is healthier than coconut chutney. You may adjust the quantity of red chillies as per your requirements/preferences. Fantastic Idly powder is ready! Now let me teach you how to prepare Podi tossed idly. Firstly, add 2 ½ tbsp of sesame oil. After it heats, add ½ tsp of mustard. It has popped well. Twist and tear a few curry leaves and add them. Turn the gas to slow, and then add just ½ tsp of the Idly powder we prepared. And toss the pre-prepared idlis into this. Toss it briefly at first so that it mixes with the oil and powder. Then continuously toss it while adding dry Milagai powder with your other hand. This will make the powder stick well to the idlis. Podi tossed idly prepared with the same Milagai powder we made! The main technique is, to first add the idlis into the oil and powder, and then continue tossing while sprinkling more powder. Only then will it mix well. Otherwise, the idlis and powder will be separate entities. Follow the aforementioned method for even coating. Hotel style Podi idly ready! Fantastic Idly Milagai powder and podi tossed idly, just for you, Venkatesh Bhat style, on Idhayam Thotta Samayal. Enjoy!

Hello and welcome to Venkatesh Bhat’s Idhayam Thotta Samayal. I will be using Idhayam Sesame oil and Idhayam Groundnut oil to prepare a wide variety of dishes. Many people have been asking about this dish for months now. Nippat in Karnataka side, and here we call it Thattai. Almost all ingredients are similar. Some people include/exclude Urad dal. But we’ll be taking 2 spoons of urad dal powder per cup of rice flour, to enhance the flavour. Some people also avoid/include garlic. I will be including it since the most important aspects of Thattai, is Hing, garlic, chopped curry leaves and soaked chana dal. Chana dal is very important, don’t add it raw. It has to soak in water for at least an hour. After soaking, it will reach a somewhat soft consistency. This must then be mixed into the dough and fried. There is a difference in the Thattai depending on whether the chana dal is raw or soaked. Soaking the dal is an important aspect to get the highest quality. I have readymade store-bought rice flour here. Light the stove and heat a kadai. I’m adding 200g of rice flour. Make sure the flame is low, because the colour of the rice flour mustn’t change. Keep stirring from all sides. This is another important technique. This will dry out any moisture content that is present in the flour. It should resemble talcum powder in dryness and softness. To prevent it from burning however, keep stirring. These small nuances are important to achieve the perfect dish. This snack is usually something we buy from outside always. But if you prepare it at home and store it in an airtight container, It will be good for up to even 15 days. There is another technique to prevent it from absorbing too much oil, i.e., the amount of water we add for mixing. See, I’ve removed the kadai from the range and am stirring it on the residual heat alone. Transfer the cooked flour to a sieve and filter it slowly so the lumps are left behind and all you get is fine rice flour. The rice flour is ready. Next, heat a kadai, and keep it on medium flame. For the 200-250g of cooked rice flour, I’m adding 3 spoon of Urad dal. Roast it on medium flame without any oil, till it turns brown colour. Roasted urad dal powder is very important in providing the right flavour for Thattai. Don’t keep the flame too high, keep it on medium so that it roasts evenly. It will take 5-7 minutes to roast to our desired colour. It has roasted evenly to a golden-brown shade. Transfer this to a cup and grind to a fine powder once it cools down. Here is the roasted urad dal powder. Add it to the kadai to remove any possible moisture content. (medium flame) for 1.5 mins. Filter the urad dal powder using a sieve, right on top of the rice flour from earlier. Observe the residual moisture filled lumps on top. We have obtained the required 2.5 spoons of urad dal powder. Take a kadai. I’m adding 1L of Mantra Groundnut oil for frying. You may take lesser depending on the size of your Kadai. Transfer both rice flour and urad dal powder to a bowl. Add required salt. A lavish sprinkle of Hing powder. (I’ve added 1 spoon) 1 spoon of Kashmiri Red Chilli powder. Since I love its flavour, I’m adding 1-1.5 tbsp of finely chopped garlic. (Optional) Add 75g of soaked Chana dal. Then take a few fresh curry leaves, roll it tightly, and chop it as fine as possible. Add it. Then, crush and add some roasted ground nut. Then, from the oil that we’ve kept for heating, take ½ ladle or 20ml of hot oil and pour it on the mixture. This is done so that the Thattai turns out crisp. Using butter instead, will make the Thattai soft. Mix well till it reaches sandy consistency. Don’t add water yet, it has to mix completely. Now, pour water little by little and continue kneading to a chapati dough consistency. It should reach a consistency where it can be rolled into balls. Pour water accordingly. If the water quantity is messed up, then it will form cracks, dissociate during frying etc. It has reached the right consistency. At the end, dab it with ½ a spoon of oil. Let it rest for 5 minutes. Roll the dough into smooth balls. Let it not be too big, because if it is thick, it won’t retain its crispiness for many days. The kadai is hot. Here I have wrapped a plastic sheet around a plate. Grease it with some oil. Add the balls one by one and flatten it to a rough round shape. Don’t let it be too thin, else it will be very fragile like a biscuit. Once flattened, immerse in the hot oil. This requires a little bit of patience; an area that I’m weak in. For example, immersing it slowly, frying slowly etc. I am frying it in medium flame slowly till it changes colour. Since it has only rice flour and urad dal powder, it is important for it to fry slowly on medium hot oil. Let it fry slowly for 8-10 minutes. Only then will all the chana dal and ground nuts roast well. So do not cook it on high flame. Occasionally flip it using your ladle. After 6-8 minutes, it will have changed colour and fried well. You can remove them. Observe the roasted groundnuts and chana dal among the golden-brown exterior! And since we’ve fried it in groundnut oil, this wonderful snack is giving out a fantastic aroma! A fantastic evening time tea snack! Serve 4 Thattais with some tea. Enjoy this fantastic evening snack, Thattai, just for you!

Hello and welcome to ‘Venkatesh Bhat’s Idhayam Thotta Samayal’ presented by Idhayam. I will be using Idhayam Sesame oil and Idhayam Groundnut oil to prepare a wide variety of dishes. In today’s episode we will be looking at Pongal and Gothsu. There were many requests for Venpongal (Khara Pongal) and Sakkarai Pongal (Sweet Pongal) I will demonstrate Venpongal Gothsu today. This is Durga Bhavan’s rendition of the recipe. Let me teach you how to prepare it. To prepare Pongal, firstly, we need to cook 2 ingredients in a cooker, Moong dal and rice. These two have to be taken in equal quantity (Ex: 1 tumbler each). You may use regular rice but for Pongal, the rice needs to cook well. For this purpose, freshly harvested rice is used. (3-4 months from time of harvest) Old rice however, will be slightly grainy even after cooking. Now, I’m taking ½ cup of Moong dal And same quantity (½ cup) of rice. Mix them up and wash them using water. Wash them for a minimum of 2-3 times. There is no requirement of soaking them, we’re going to add them directly to the cooker. But before that, it must be washed 2-3 times. The water straining step is very important. Make sure to strain it completely. Add the mixture to the cooker. Now take the same vessel you used to measure moong dal and rice for adding the water. It is very important for Pongal to have the right water content to turn out good. This is where people make mistakes They either add a lot of water or add very little of it. So, the right water content is essential to achieve the optimum consistency. Now with respect to this cup, I’m pouring 3 ¾ cups of water. (Keep in mind I added half cup each of Moong dal and rice) To this, add ¼ spoon of ghee. Close the lid and light the stove. Let it cook for 3 whistles. (8-10 minutes) After 3 whistles are done, let it rest for 10 minutes. Don’t take out the whistle and lid because the cooking process won’t be complete. Only after letting it rest, will the Pongal cook appropriately. So, I’m going to let it cook for 3 whistles. Before that, we look at how to prepare Gothsu, which is a fantastic combo for Pongal. There are many recipes for Gothsu which utilize brinjals, tomato, with/without onion or even with/without Moong dal. So, there are many recipes. I will teach you the recipe that I’m familiar with. It utilizes Moong dal, onion, tomato etc. A powder has to be prepared for it. Let us look at how to prepare both the powder and the Gothsu. Before that, I’m going to let this cook for 3 whistles. Now, light the stove and take a pan. I’m adding 1 tsp of Mantra Groundnut oil. 2 ½ tsp of gram dal. (Keep the gas on low flame) 1 ½ tsp of urad dal. 2 tsp of Dhaniya seeds. 8 round red chillies. Roast everything well. To this, add ¼ tsp of fenugreek seeds. (Don’t add too much, it will be bitter) Turn off the gas when it has roasted well. Before transferring it, add little more than ½ a tsp of Hing. Mix well. Transfer to another vessel. Once it cools down, it is to be ground into a fine powder. Now let’s see how to prepare the Gothsu. I have Idhayam Sesame oil here. Sesame oil is best for this. I’ve added 2 tbsp of Sesame oil. Little mustard. It has to pop. Some curry leaves. 75g of small peeled onions. I’m adding them directly, you may cut them if you wish. Let the onion cook well. To people who don’t want onion in the Gothsu, you may skip this and directly add tomato. Some people don’t add tomato as well, so follow whichever recipe is appropriate for your requirements. Many people have asked questions about where to buy knives, how to maintain them etc. I don’t give my knives for sharpening regardless of whether they’re from India or abroad. The temper of a knife is very important. There is a connection between the steel, knife and the grip. They’re all in proportion to each other with respect to scientific calculations. So, if we sharpen the knife using grindstone etc. the temper of the knife will be altered. It will be sharp for 14 days but turn blunt after that. And you will have to send it for sharpening again. So, for home knives, follow this method. Take a knife like so in your left hand and make the blunt side face your cutting knife which is in right hand. Rub the sharp side of the cutting knife to the blunt side of the other knife. Even if you do it just 10 times, It will remain sharp for another couple days. The onions have turned slightly brown. At this stage, chop one tomato like so and add it. Add ½ tsp of turmeric powder. I have some brinjals here. You may use any type of brinjal. There is no major difference. Chop the brinjals like so into small cubes. If the cubes are too big, it won’t be pleasant to eat. It is important for the brinjals to cook well. Some people burn the brinjal directly by keeping it on a flame. They then use the mashed burnt brinjal to prepare the Gothsu. That will also be fantastic because of its smoky flavour. You may opt for that as well. At this stage, add the brinjal. You may slightly increase the flame now. Pour some water for the ingredients to cook well. It will take about 5-7 minutes of cooking on high flame. Don’t add salt yet, it is to be added in the end. Whenever you cook brinjal, add salt at the end because otherwise it won’t cook well. So, the brinjal, onion and tomato have to boil well amongst the turmeric powder for another 5 minutes. All the ingredients have cooked well. At this stage, add 1 ¼ ladle of thick tamarind water. (50g of tamarind soaked in hot water and squeezed) You will get double the quantity of tamarind water I just added. (provided you follow the same measurements) You may store the remaining quantity after adding half of it. At this stage, add the required salt. Add 1 tsp of crushed jaggery. You may skip this if you wish. This is for the sake of light sweetness in the dish. Each ingredient is important for the final taste of the dish, so I’m teaching it the way I learnt it. Okay, now everything has cooked well. At this stage, take the powder which we ground earlier, and add 2 tsp of it. The gram dal and urad dal will thicken the whole mixture. For people who wish to skip the addition of Moong dal, you may turn off the gas now and Gothsu is ready. But as per the recipe, add 100g of boiled moong. Pour a tumbler of water. The gothsu for Pongal shouldn’t be too thick. It should be thicker than sambar but not as thick as kurma. That is the reason behind the addition of moong. See the colour! It is somewhat similar to sambar since it has ingredients like onion, tomato, powder etc. Bring it to a slight boil and add a lavish sprinkle of coriander. Don’t let it boil for too long. That’s it, gothsu is ready! On the other hand, the moong dal and rice mixture has finished cooking for 3 whistles and has been allowed to rest for 10 minutes. Let’s see the further process of preparing Pongal from it. The moong dal and rice mixture has finished cooking for 3 whistles and has been allowed to rest for 10 minutes. I’m removing the whistle since the steam has dissipated. Observe, this is how it should be cooked. As I’ve said before, use measurements with respect to the measurement cup that you’re using. It will turn out well like this. Now, take a pan to prepare the seasoning for the Pongal. We usually use Vanaspati in hotels because it is the most appropriate to prepare Pongal. But I will avoid using it since many of you might have a problem with Vanaspati. I will be using regular ghee. Everyone close your eyes else you’ll be shocked if you see how much ghee I’m adding! The rice and moong dal together add up to around 500-600g. For that, I’ve added 100g of ghee. This is the right quantity for how I prefer to eat Pongal. You may reduce the quantity or skip it altogether if you wish to. Keep in mind that health complications aren’t always in our hand and aren’t directly linked to food always. So even if you prepare it rarely, prepare it the right way. If you prepare it frequently then don’t use this much ghee. The most important for Pongal is the tempering since it is the determining factor for the final taste. There are 3 important things: one, make sure that the curry leaves are tender and fresh and not wilted. Two, Hing. The combination of Hing and curry leaves decides the fate of the Pongal. Thirdly, ginger. Be sure to peel the ginger completely else it will be bitter. So, these small tricks are very important for the final result of the Pongal. Firstly, after the ghee is heated, add 1 ¼ tsp of pepper. The cooker I have used has a quantity of 600g so the ingredients for this are with respect to that. Let the pepper pop. I have been preparing Pongal for 25 years but I still called my father to confirm the recipe. He told me to keep my distance after adding the pepper and I’m repeating the same to you. Add ¾ tsp of Jeera. Add 30-40g of peeled and chopped ginger. After the raw smell goes away, be generous when adding cashew nuts. The objective is to get one cashew with every spoonful of Pongal. If you prefer, you may reduce the quantity or skip it altogether. Meanwhile, I have Asafoetida gum here. It is from Afghanistan. For Pongal, it is better to use this type Asafoetida/Hing. It is magic. Soak it in hot water for 30 mins and then squeeze it. After squeezing you may even store this in your fridge for more than a week. It will be excellent if used for Sambar etc. After it turns golden brown, add 30ml (3 tbsp) of thick Hing water. (Make sure not to let the squeezed water rest even for a second) Add a handful of fresh curry leaves. Increase the intensity of the flame and mix well so that the curry leaves and Hing water mix and boil well. That’s it, turn off the gas. It has roasted properly. Observe the curry leaves, it is still fresh, but it has soaked in oil as well. Add it to the rice and moong dal mixture. Add the required salt for Pongal. Mix well so that all the ingredients harmonize with each other. Add some ghee on top. Close the lid and keep it aside. Don’t disturb it for 20 minutes. Plate the gothsu. Thicker than sambar, but not as thick as kurma. This is the right consistency. Garnish with some coriander. Aha! One small technology, wrap the ladle with cling foil or polythene cover/milk packet cover using a rubber band. This is so that the Pongal comes off smoothly. It is sitting there like a ball! Today I'm making a Quick One-Pan Dinner: juicy chicken breast with fried cabbage and spaghetti Stir Fry. Why haven't I used ground chicken instead of chicken fillet before? It's so delicious Stir Fry! If you have cabbage, chicken breast, and vegetables at home, make this quick and easy dish. All the ingredients are cooked in one skillet. I add the spaghetti and cook it right in the skillet. It's simple and delicious. The spaghetti absorbs the flavor of the cabbage and carrots. I add a little soy sauce and sweet chili sauce. The combination of chicken, cabbage, and spaghetti in one skillet is simply amazing! You'll love this quick and delicious cabbage recipe. I adore this cabbage and ground chicken dish. It's so easy to make! This delicious, filling, and healthy dinner will delight your whole family. I love quick one-skillet recipes. Happy cooking!

🥣🥣🥣 Ingredients:
1 cabbage.
1 chicken fillet.
1 onion.
1 carrot.
A handful of the thinnest spaghetti.
Pour in 1/2 a glass of water.
3 cloves of garlic.
1 tablespoon of sweet chili sauce.
2 tablespoons of soy sauce.
Spring onions.
Salt.
1.5 tablespoons of butter.
Enjoy your meal 😋!
